summary: Hōkai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hōgetsu and Zuihe.
Hōkei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, where he was attested as a professor in 1930.

Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Cambridge and Lancaster University, he held posts at Lancaster, the Becket Institute, Oxford, NUS, and the University of Cumbria (~1999–2014), where he was Professor Emeritus.

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and was attested in 2005 as a research fellow at Monash University.
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He later taught Shunryu Suzuki.

Ian Reader (b. 1949) specializes in Japanology and religious studies. After completing his doctorate at the University of Leeds (~1978–1983), he held posts at Kobe University of Commerce, Kansai Gaidai, Stirling, Hawaii, and Lancaster University (~2002–2009).

Ibrahim Shah is a scholar of history and archaeology. He completed his PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar under Muhammad Farooq Swati in 2007 and served as Associate Professor and Department Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa (b. 1936) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959) and later served on its faculty (~1971–2007), as well as at Otani University Junior College (attested 1978).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies and archaeology scholar. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935), he held posts at Nishogakusha, Kokugakuin, Tohoku University (~1952–1965), University of Tokyo (~1965–1971), and Seijo University (~1971–1974).
Ichiro Katayama (b. 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1962–1966) and later served there as a professor from ~1990 to 2013.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Sapienza University of Rome (~1864–1869) and later held a post there from ~1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University (~1936–1941), he held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, Pravda, and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1961–1998).

Ikko Arai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Komazawa University under Shiro Matsumoto. He also studied under Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen, Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.

Ikuhisa Takigawa (b. 1968) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Waseda University, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University and Tokai University, both attested in 2002.
Ikuko Tazaki is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, she held posts as a special researcher at Otani University and as a collaborative researcher at Kyoto University.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (b. 1959) is a religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki under René Gothóni, where he served as an Academy Research Fellow in 1984, and was later a visiting researcher at Oxford.

Imre Galambos (b. 1967) is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. Educated at ELTE, Nankai, and UC Berkeley (PhD 2002), he held posts at UC Santa Barbara, the British Library (~2002–2012), Ryukoku University, and the University of Cambridge (2012).

Imre Hamar (b. 1967) works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and National Taiwan Normal University under advisor Noritoshi Aramaki, he became Professor of Chinese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University and visited Otani University.

In-gun Kang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, the Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, and Heythrop College, where he completed a doctorate under Michael Barnes.

Ines Konczak is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as a postdoctoral research fellow at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University (2012).
